question: Usain Bolt shared the journey of his life in which of the following autobiographies?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Faster Than Lightning**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• It chronicles Usain Bolt's journey from his humble beginnings in rural Jamaica to becoming a global sports icon.
 
• The autobiography delves into his childhood, revealing the influences that shaped his character and athletic abilities.
 
• It provides insights into his early experiences with sports, including cricket, before he focused on track and field.
 
• The book documents his rise through the ranks of athletics, from his early successes in junior competitions to his record-breaking performances at the Olympic Games and World Championships.
 
• It offers a behind-the-scenes look at his training regimen, the challenges he faced, and the dedication required to achieve his goals.
 
• Bolt shares his thoughts and feelings about his most memorable races, including his world record-setting performances.
 
• The autobiography also explores his personality, his sense of humor, and his approach to life.
 
• It gives readers a look into the pressures of being a world famous athlete.
 
• It details the work with his coaches that helped him become the fastest man in the world.
 
• It tells of his experiences at the olympic games, and the world championships.
 
• It shows the readers, the development of his world record times.
 
• The book details his life outside of track and field, and his personal life.
 
• The book was released in 2013.
 
• It was published by HarperSport.
 
• The book was co-written with Matt Allen.
 
• It has been published in many different languages.
 
• The book gives insight into the Jamaican culture, that helped create Usain Bolt.
 
• The book shows how his family life, helped to shape his character.
 
• The book gives a very personal look into the life of Usain Bolt.
 
• The book is very popular among sports fans.
 
• It is considered to be a very inspiring book.
